target_customer: Knowledge workers and teams who want automatic tracking of how they spend time on computers
problem: People could not see where their working hours went; manual timesheets were unreliable.
business_model: Freemium SaaS, paid premium and team plans
product_category: Automatic time tracking and productivity analytics

founders.name: Brian Fioca
founders.background_notes: YC page: product engineer with 20+ years of experience, founded 5 companies including RescueTime. Some directories name Tony Wright, Joe Hruska or Mark Wolgemuth as co-founders; no YC or company source confirms, so not listed.

competitors.name: Slife
competitors.what: Automatic desktop activity tracking with online data visualization

competitors.name: Wakoopa
competitors.what: Web service tracking software usage on your computer

technical_complexity.rationale: Desktop agents on Windows and Mac that log active windows plus a web dashboard; categorization of activity was the main work.

defensibility.rationale: Several lookalike trackers existed; accumulated categorization data and installed agents gave small lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Operating systems later added built-in screen time tools; RescueTime stayed independent and no acquirer found.

market_need_then: Early 2008 blog coverage grouped RescueTime with Slife and Wakoopa as tools to track computer activity, showing interest in automatic time tracking.

identity.logo: Originally red; redesigned after a letter from the Red Cross about the red emblem
identity.voice_and_tone: Take back control of your time; less busywork, more meaningful work

branding.brand_signature: Take back control of your time tagline
branding.community_and_virality: PC Mag Editor's Choice; testimonial from Alexis Ohanian; company blog covers its logo redesign.

brand_strength.rationale: Evocative name that explains the benefit and steady press, but the red logo dispute shows a minor brand setback and no fan culture is documented.

outcome_analysis: RescueTime pioneered automatic time tracking, raised about 900K from True Ventures and angels in 2008 plus a 2011 raise, and reached 2 million users. It remained a small private company of about 11 to 15 people; a 2025 community thread suggests slowed product development, but no sale or shutdown is reported.
notes: Totals conflict: CB Insights 920K, GeekWire 2011 says total 1.1M, PitchBook 2.02M; the 2011 round amount is not stated in what I opened and is left null (gap vs PitchBook unresolved).
